Package gooeygui

Class Component

java.lang.Object
gooeygui.Component
Direct Known Subclasses:
Button, CheckBox, Dropdown, Image, Label, Panel, RadioButton, Slider, TabbedPane, TextArea, TextField
public abstract class Component extends Object
The parent class of every visual GooeyGUI component, such as Button, Label, and TextField. The methods listed here can be called on any of those components.

Every component has a position and a size, measured in pixels. The position (x, y) is the top-left corner of the component, measured from the top-left corner of the Window or Panel that contains it. The x-coordinate increases to the right and the y-coordinate increases downward.

Component cannot be created directly. Create one of its subclasses instead:


 Button myButton = new Button("Click me", 50, 100, 120, 30);
 myButton.setX(200);   // works on every kind of component

    • setEnabled

      public void setEnabled(boolean isEnabled)
      Enables or disables the component. A disabled component is still visible but appears grayed out and cannot be clicked or edited by the user. Components are enabled by default.

      Disabling a Panel or TabbedPane also disables everything inside it. Enabling it again restores each inner component to its own setting, so a button you disabled yourself stays disabled.

      Parameters:
      isEnabled - true to let the user interact with the component, false to prevent interaction

    • isEnabled

      public boolean isEnabled()
      Returns the value last given to setEnabled(boolean) for this component. This does not check whether a containing Panel is disabled.
      Returns:
      true if this component is enabled, false otherwise

    • setActive

      public void setActive(boolean isActive)
      Shows or hides the component. An inactive component is invisible, so the user cannot see or use it. Components are active by default.

      Hiding a Panel or TabbedPane also hides everything inside it. Showing it again restores each inner component to its own setting, so a button you hid yourself stays hidden.

      Parameters:
      isActive - true to show the component, false to hide it

    • isActive

      public boolean isActive()
      Returns the value last given to setActive(boolean) for this component. This does not check whether a containing Panel is hidden.
      Returns:
      true if this component is active, false otherwise
